column6: Ungating lt_sync_store armed inference on the CS2 lanes, and the pass then wrote source_count = count from the record -- so the FIRST thing the record took erased every band inference had settled. Measured: infer an Imp kill (detail 'Imp', 21 gp), let the record take a Goblin, strip is 126px; the same record with nothing inferred beside it is ALSO 126px. Identical, because the Imp band was gone. Same family as LOOTTRACKER-LIVE-IGNORES-A-FED-STORE: a page asserting what it has no basis for. column5: test_loot_a_cheat_kill_does_not_disable_inference; mutation 'record holds anything' for 'holds this name' -> 2 failures
column6: The record has two feeders: CS2_OP_LOOT_ADD (the game's own, CS2 script lanes only) and App_LootNotifyKill (::lootkill, every lane). On the 2004 lane the cheat is the ONLY writer, so a latch reading 'the record has taken something, stop inferring' turned one ::lootkill into a permanent, silent switch-off of that lane's only account of a real kill. Measured: seed one ::lootkill, then kill an Imp -- strip 126px, one band, still 'Goblin'. Documented in a comment, asserted nowhere. The latch (record_kept) is deleted; the question is per source now.

column5: test_loot_an_inferred_band_is_not_the_records_band; mutation `++g_next_fallback_source_id` -> 3 failures
column6: LootStore numbers its sources from 1 (rs_loot_store.c: store->next_source_id = 1) and the bands the plugin invents were numbered from 1 too -- safe only while the two accounts could never be on the page together. Merging them made a recorded Goblin and an inferred Imp share id 1, and the id is what a click, a band menu and the detail block all key on: pressing the Imp band opened the GOBLIN's detail, 5,000 gp of coins under the word 'Imp'. Found by the merge, not reported by anyone. Inferred ids now start at LT_INFERRED_ID_BASE (1<<24) and lt_sync_store asserts the record stays below it.

column6: THE SYMPTOM WAS REAL AND THE STATED CAUSE WAS NOT. `grep PLUGIN_NOTIFY runs/` over 307 captures returned nothing from this builtin, and the reading offered was that the 2-tick grace loses to cannon.rs2's own "Your cannon is out of ammunition!" on every OSRS239 lane. That half is correct and is the REPAIR, not the defect: nxt_cannon_chat dropping the duplicate is what fixes a photographed two-lines-for-one-event bug, and nothing in the plugin needed changing. What actually kept it silent was the DRIVE. Its other message, the low-on-ammo one, is not pre-empted by anything -- no content anywhere sends a low line -- and it was unreachable twice over: setting 249 (varbit 14176, the amount) has no default and the job rows never wrote it, so `threshold > 0` was false for ever; and the only ammo change in the drive was loc op 3 "Empty", a one-tick 15 -> 0 that has no intermediate value for a threshold to be crossed at. docs/plugin-engine/PLUGIN_PORTS.md had said all along that this drive writes 14175=1, 14176=10, 14177=1 -- the job files shipped two of the three. Fixed in the drive: 14176=10, plus `::spawn goblin 20` so the cannon fires its count down one ball a tick, 4000 frames. All four toplevels now log exactly one PLUGIN_NOTIFY ("running low on cannonballs: 10 left.") and still zero "run out of cannonballs", which is both halves in one chat pane

column6: OBSERVATION right, DIAGNOSIS wrong, and the shot's subject is not the chat pane. (a) NOT A RACE. The pane is covered whenever the shot's derived LostCity account is NEW: login.rs2 runs @start_tutorial only while %tutorial < ^tutorial_complete AND the player stands on tutorial island, both true on a first login and never again, and the box tut_open raises lives in the engine's TUT modal slot, which if_close cannot empty -- Player.closeModal clears modalMain/modalChat/modalSide and only Player.closeTutorial writes TutOpen(-1) -- so ~skiptutorial's if_close leaves it standing for the whole run. st_birthtime settles the counter-example the report leaned on: snxthl_live born 21:07:20 and photographed at 23:34 (clear); scannon_liv born 23:37:24, inside its own capture (covered). Of the 47 live captures taken on this lane's own 2004 frame, 37 are the first kind and the 10 clear ones are exactly those whose account predates the sweep; control-live is one of the 37, which is why a control diff could not see it. The controlled pair runs ONE drive, ONE binary and ONE account name twice: nxt5freshA (first login) CHAT_REGION iface=6179 tut_com=6179 log_visible=0; nxt5freshB (same account, second login) log_visible=1. (b) UNCOVERING IT PHOTOGRAPHS NOTHING ANYWAY. rev289lc declares neither varbit:bird_nest nor varp:cannon_coord, so both plugins' Porcelain_Require refuses at start, available stays false and no sampler is registered -- each run log says so twice as a PORCELAIN_FINDING on frame 0 -- and neither live drive produces a nest or a cannon in the first place (~torirsdrop is a scimitar, a helm, coins and sharks; there is no cannon cheat on this server). What was REAL here is HARNESS-01 below: nothing in the harness could see the covered pane. The client now writes CHAT_REGION beside every BMP and live_check.py fails on it

UITree_NodeSubtreePaintsArt walks down from a node the caller has already found presented, asks UITree_EmitFill (the emit pass's own verdict, so scene_id<=0, hitbox-only and the placeholder types are all folded in) and stops at the first descriptor that is not text. MEASURED on the report button, which answers presented=true and graphic_token=0 on all four: classic548 FALSE, classic161 FALSE, modern164 TRUE, native548 TRUE -- the art is on a child, and the 2004 provider hides that child when it draws the cells into its own chat-bar rock. screenshot.lua brings the plate only where that is true; where it is false the camera takes the target's place as it did before f033da98f. The slab is GONE from the 2004 stone (fixes/sshot-plate-classic548-compare.png, the button box at 8x: A the plate, B this change, C the lane with no plugin) and modern164 is unmoved (fixes/sshot-plate-modern164-after.png). It is a text child of the target, and REPLACE consumes it on native548 (the whole button goes, art and caption) and does NOT on classic548/161 -- measured, both placements: a camera anchored REPLACE and a camera anchored INSIDE produce the SAME picture there, with the caption cutting straight through the icon, so the caption is not in the record list the anchor reorder rewrites on that lane. Hiding that one child by hand is the owner's remembered picture exactly (fixes/sshot-plate-classic548-caption-hidden.png) but the plugin may not reach it: no porcelain element names it, and raw set_hidden on this subtree is the shape the port retired (screenshot_behavior.lua refuses it). THE ASYMMETRY WAS A LAYER BUG AND IT IS FIXED. Traced in the anchor plan: on native548 the camera's unit carries relation REPLACE and the target's THREE records (the button, its art child, its caption) are dropped for it; on classic548 a REPLACE appeared on one build and the very next one -- the fence the provider's `layout Classic Fixed` line prints -- came back with replaces=0, the same unit count, and the camera anchored OVER. The cause is porcelain_apply_anchor's early-out, which compared only the anchor TARGET: this plugin's camera stands INSIDE the button while it paints its own plate and REPLACES it once a frame provider hides that plate, so the ref is identical across the switch and the layer decided there was nothing to write. The control kept OVER for the rest of the session and the records the REPLACE was there to consume went on being drawn -- which is why the caption cut through the camera, and why no placement could get over it. The relation is now remembered beside the target (PorcelainAppliedItem::anchor_relation) and either one moving re-writes the anchor; an unchanged pair still costs no setter, which the same test pins. column6: Porcelain_Derived recomposing a key at a NEW SIZE hands back a new ToriRS_ImageRef, but the applied control keeps its old one: porcelain_apply_properties re-resolves only when the image NAME changes, and Porcelain_Image caches name->handle and never re-asks once READY. Porcelain_ImageForget is documented for exactly this and is called from nowhere in porcelain*.c. Not reachable today (the report button is 79x23 on 548/161/164 and absent on 601); needs a runtime toplevel switch to a differently-sized button

column6: remount548 is NON-DETERMINISTIC about whether the lane re-mounts interface 729 after the 164->548 switch, so its BOUNDS count varies by 17 between runs of the SAME binary. A gate lane that answers differently twice teaches people to discount the gate, which is worse than not having the lane -- it cost an integration one false regression investigation already. Either the capture must wait for the remount to settle, or the comparison must not count an interface whose mounting the drive does not determine

A diff that reports motion where nothing moved is the same disease as GATE-02 in a milder form
